cmad.notes: PROBA2 is an ESA mission, not subject to the NASA senior-review CMAD requirement, so a CMAD is not expected and its absence is unremarkable. No CMAD was located via general web search either. Proceeded with the remaining sources (record Contacts, sibling Instrument records, mission overview paper, provider pages).

instrument_coverage.notes: Observatory records carry no downward instrument links; roster established by reverse lookup of https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/PROBA2/ (found DSLP, LYRA, SWAP, TPMU, each with ObservatoryID=spase://SMWG/Observatory/PROBA2 confirmed) and cross-checked against the observatory record's own Description, which lists five experiments: SWAP, LYRA, TPMU, DSLP, and SGVM (Science Grade Vector Magnetometer). SGVM has no SPASE Instrument record. Per skill, its team was pursued externally: web search shows SGVM was developed by the Technical University of Denmark as a technology-demonstrator/attitude-support instrument; no named PI surfaced in the fetched sources, so no candidate was minted for it. SGVM flagged for curators as a metadata gap.

notes: Record type: Observatory (spase://SMWG/Observatory/PROBA2). ESA mission launched 2 Nov 2009, still operating. The observatory record has NO OperatingSpan element; operating_span.start (2009-11-02) is inferred from the record Description (launch date) and stop=null from the mission still producing data (e.g. the LYRA Flarelist data record). Downstream should treat the span as inferred, not authoritative.
CMAD not expected: ESA mission, outside NASA senior-review CMAD requirement. See cmad object.

Instrument reverse-lookup: SPASE has 4 instrument records (LYRA, SWAP, DSLP, TPMU), each ObservatoryID-verified against PROBA2. The record Description enumerates 5 experiments; SGVM (Science Grade Vector Magnetometer, built by Technical University of Denmark, an attitude-support/technology-demonstrator instrument) has NO SPASE record. No named SGVM PI surfaced, so no candidate minted for it. Flagged in instrument_coverage.missing_from_spase for curators.

Observatory description paper = mission overview 'PROBA2: Mission and Spacecraft Overview' (doi:10.1007/s11207-013-0289-5, Solar Physics 2013). Paper selection CONFIDENT: title keyword 'Overview', 12-author whole-team list, 54 citations, and 2013 publication ~3.5 yr after the 2009 launch (within the 2-5 yr window). Crossref is authoritative; no conflicting candidate paper. Position-based evidence therefore used at full weight.

Mission overview author list contains two consortium/team names as 'authors': 'PROBA2 Project Team' (first overall) and 'PROBA2 Industry Team' (interspersed). Per skill, team names generate no candidate and transfer no position boost. Named-person contribution order is: 1 Santandrea, 2 Gantois, 3 Strauch, 4 Teston, 5 Tilmans, 6 Baijot, 7 Gerrits, 8 De Groof, 9 Schwehm, 10 Zender. Backward alphabetization scan on named persons found no sorted suffix of >=5 (Zender, Schwehm, De Groof, Gerrits, Baijot ... not sorted) => NOT alphabetized; position used as contribution signal. Positions 1-3 Strong, 4-5 Medium taken.

SWAP instrument description paper (doi:10.1007/978-1-4614-8187-4_4, 20 authors) is PARTIALLY ALPHABETIZED: backward scan found a sorted suffix of 11 beginning at position 10 (Auchere, Defise, D'Huys, Lecat, Mazy, Rochus, Rossi, Schuhle, Slemzin, Yalim, Zender), so the deliberate prefix = positions 1-9 (Seaton, Berghmans, Nicula, Halain, De Groof, Thibert, Bloomfield, Raftery, Gallagher). Prefix positional weighting applied within positions 1-5.

Scoping decision: for this Observatory record, included instrument candidates are each instrument's lead(s) - the SPASE Instrument-record PI and (where different) the instrument description-paper lead. SWAP therefore contributes Berghmans (PI) and Seaton (paper lead). SWAP prefix members Nicula (pos3) and Halain (pos4) are NOT swept into the observatory list - they belong to the SWAP Instrument-record's own author-finding run and are recorded as excluded so the trail is visible. De Groof is the exception: included at Medium because she appears in BOTH the SWAP prefix (pos5) AND the mission overview paper (two independent description papers) and is the ESA PROBA2 project scientist.

SWAP alphabetized-tail authors (F. Auchere, J.-M. Defise, E. D'Huys, J.-H. Lecat, E. Mazy, P. Rochus, L. Rossi, U. Schuhle, V. Slemzin, M. S. Yalim, J. Zender) carry no position evidence and are not listed individually; they are participation-level only and belong to SWAP-instrument scope. Likewise LYRA paper co-authors beyond the lead (J.-F. Hochedez, W. Schmutz, I. E. Dammasch, A. I. Shapiro, M. Kretzschmar) are LYRA-instrument scope, not observatory candidates.

DSLP PI Pavel M. Travenicek and TPMU PI Frantisek Hruska rest on the Instrument-record qualifying role only (Medium). No DSLP/TPMU description paper was fetched to corroborate; downstream may wish to confirm. Both have existing Person records.

None of the mission-overview named authors (Santandrea, Gantois, Strauch, Teston, Tilmans, Baijot, Gerrits, Schwehm) have SMWG Person records (all 404). The four instrument PIs, Joe Zender, Daniel B. Seaton, and Anik De Groof all have Person records.
Name-form caveat: SWAP paper lists 'D. B. Seaton'; matched to existing Person record Daniel.B.Seaton (given initial D. = Daniel). Downstream should confirm identity.
